Closes #19063

## Summary

The comment lint's CI re-run was a hand-copied README recipe, and this repository ran its own GitHub-only wrapper (`scripts/check-comment-lint.sh`, keyed on `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `HEAD_SHA` and `BASE_REF`). This ships one CI-neutral script in the plugin and a guided `/code-tidying:setup apply install-ci` that discovers the repository's CI system and proposes the step in that system's own format, with no CI system as a default and no vendor template, as the owner asked on 2026-11-25.

## Fix

- `plugins/code-tidying/git-hooks/comment-lint-ci.sh <head> <base>`: both commits as arguments, no vendor variable. Adds a detached worktree at the head without checking files out (the lint reads the index, so the repository's files never land on disk), soft-resets to the merge base, restores `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the home's `code-tidying.yaml`/`code-tidying.local.yaml` from the merge base, runs `comment-lint.sh` from beside itself, removes the worktree; exits with the lint's status, 2 on usage. Listed as an asset in `entries.json`, so a shared hook install commits it under `.githooks/code-tidying/` where a consumer's CI can call it.
- `plugins/code-tidying/scripts/comment-lint-ci-scan.py`: read-only JSON for the setup agent: CI systems found by their configuration files (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI, Bitbucket and others), task-runner files, which files name `python3`/pygments, callers of the script (arguments parsed through template expressions and continued lines) or of the older recipe, and `decisions[]` (`no-ci-system`, `several-systems`, `no-caller`, `recipe-caller`, `drift`, `unparsed`, `unreached-caller`, `missing-tool`), mirroring the installer's plan shape. A commented-out line is never a caller, and a caller in a make, task or just target counts only when an uncommented CI line runs that target; otherwise it is `unreached-caller` (not installed).
- Setup skill: new `apply install-ci` (discover, stop when present, ask only what discovery leaves open, propose in the system's format and the repository's conventions, write only on a yes, print for a system it cannot write); `check` step 10 reports the caller, drift and `unreached-caller` as a FAIL, the recipe as INFO. New `reference/ci-systems.md`: what the step does in any system, where the script comes from, and an instruction to read the named system's own documentation at run time. It links no vendor page: docs/plugin-philosophy.md "No ecosystem-specific examples" bars "a link to one tool's documentation" in a shipped reference file and makes no exception for a side-by-side list, so the vendor table was removed. The `no-ci-rerun` decision now offers `apply install-ci`.
- This repository: `pr-require-checks.yml`'s comment-lint step calls the shipped script (`"$HEAD_SHA" "origin/$BASE_REF"`, pull_request only, as before); `scripts/check-comment-lint.sh` and its test are deleted (its cases moved to `comment-lint-ci.test.sh`); the `check-script-contract` registry row and `check-affected.sh`'s description follow.
- README: the recipe is replaced by how `apply install-ci` works and the script's interface. Changelog fragment `bump: minor`. No default or setting changed.

## Verification

- `plugins/code-tidying/git-hooks/comment-lint-ci.test.sh`: 23 checks pass, every case of the deleted `check-comment-lint.test.sh` (base level wins, home rename, planted symlink, base moving ahead) plus a flat copy laid out like an installed hook, an ADR pointer with no files checked out, and the usage errors.
- `test_comment_lint_ci_scan.py`: 25 tests pass (vendor detection, template expressions, continued lines, Groovy quoting, drift, recipe callers, missing tool, commented-out callers, and reach: the review repro of a `.gitlab-ci.yml` running only `make test` beside a Makefile `comment-lint` target reports `unreached-caller`; make, just and task targets a CI line runs are reached).
- `comment-lint.test.sh` (72), `lib/git-hooks/sh-entries.test.sh` (254; caught a bare `bash` call in the new asset, fixed), `lefthook-remote.test.sh`, `install.test.sh`, `check-affected*.test.sh`: pass on the merged head.
- The 61 suites that read `pr-require-checks.yml`: 57 pass; `run-hygiene-gate.test.sh` and `ci-test-node-stop-commands.test.sh` pass when rerun with a `python3` that has PyYAML; `callers.test.mjs` and `admit.test.mjs` could not load `ajv`/`yaml` (no `node_modules` in this worktree), left to CI. `check-script-contract.test.sh` fails only its `check-html-assets` rows for the same missing `node_modules`.
- Dogfood: `bash plugins/code-tidying/git-hooks/comment-lint-ci.sh HEAD origin/main` on this branch exits 0; the scan on this repository reports one `script` caller, `pr-require-checks.yml`, args `$HEAD_SHA origin/$BASE_REF`, no drift.
- `scripts/check-changed-skills.sh origin/main`: PASS (5 size warnings; the body was already over the router cap before this change, the procedure moved to `actions/install-ci.md`). `scripts/check-changelog-fragments.sh --check-required origin/main`: pass.

## Related

- `scripts/check-affected.sh` keeps its own local variant of the merge-base lint (a scratch repository over alternates), unchanged here.

pullRequest.body:
Closes #18577

## Summary

Opened by the work-resolve-issue lane. The run's own summary:

> reference-verify.sh now builds one verifier payload per changed file into a batch directory and starts run-guards.sh once per range in a new `--batch <dir>` mode. That mode sources hook-utils.sh once, then runs the unchanged single-payload chain on each payload in a forked subshell (`(source run-guards.sh <guards>) <N.in >N.out`, status to N.rc), so each file pays a fork instead of a bash start plus a 253 KB library parse. Design choice and basis: the recorded decision (issue comment, 2026-11-25) narrows the issue to proposed step 3, and run-guards.sh's header says guards share globals in one process, so a fork per payload keeps each payload's state isolated while hook-utils.sh's and abort-boundary.sh's double-source guards (`_HOOK_UTILS_LOADED`, `_GUARDRAILS_ABORT_BOUNDARY_LOADED`) make the child's own source lines no-ops. Hook rows never pass `--batch`, so the edit-time path only adds one `\[\[ \]\]` test. Findings keep `<path>:<line>` attribution and are reported in file order; a file whose batch slot has a non-zero or missing status is reported unchecked and fails the check.

## Not verified

- reference-verify.test.sh, stale-path-verify.test.sh and run-guards.test.sh were not executed: this lane's Bash runs only the named wrappers, so the suites are left to the PR's CI.
- No before/after timing on Linux or Windows Git Bash: no Windows host here and no way to run the script in this lane. The decision's acceptance criteria do not require it; the original issue's measurement criteria are superseded by the recorded decision.
- check-affected skipped comment-hygiene (network fetch denied), size-check (script absent in the lane checkout), typos (not installed), reference-verify and lint-full (not present in the lane's check tree); these run in CI.
- tidy: hooks/run-guards.sh was dropped from tidy (it is a hook command, on the GLOBAL HARD list under enforce); the ai-slop detector script could not run (lane Bash allows only named wrappers), so the fragment got a rubric read only.
- Untracked dotfiles at the checkout root (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .gitconfig, .idea, .mcp.json, .profile, .ripgreprc, .vscode, .zprofile, .zshrc) are not from this run; they look like sandbox mount placeholders and must not go into the patch.
- verify step: no build or test run was possible in this lane beyond the checks above.

## Fix

- plugins/guardrails/hooks/run-guards.sh: new `--batch <dir>` entry before the abort boundary: sources hook-utils.sh once, runs the chain per `<dir>/<i>.in` in a forked subshell, writes `<i>.out` and `<i>.rc`.
- plugins/guardrails/git-hooks/reference-verify.sh: check_range builds all payloads first (per-file notes for read/list/jq-build failures), runs one `run-guards.sh --batch` per range, then reads each slot's status and output in file order; a missing or non-zero status reports that file unchecked.
- plugins/guardrails/git-hooks/reference-verify.test.sh: counting wrapper now logs each start and reads the batch payloads; new case: a --base range of four changed files starts the verifiers once, judges all four, and names run.sh:3; new case: a forced status 3 on one batch slot reports that file…
- plugins/guardrails/README.md: reference-verify runs through one `hooks/run-guards.sh --batch` process per range.
- .changes/guardrails/work-resolve-issue-issue-18577-45624484385-1-7c810f41.md: patch fragment (Changed) for the batching.

## Verification

The runner ran each check from the base copy against 0f389f684dcb6c61c04c539389cff2b457203487:

- scripts/check-changelog-fragments.sh --check: passed
- scripts/check-changed-skills.sh --merge-base: passed

The run reports:

- check-changelog-fragments: all 38 fragments valid
- check-changed-skills: no changed skills, nothing to gate
- check-affected: 17 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed (first run failed comment-lint on two edited comment lines in reference-verify.sh's report() header; reverted those edits and re-ran clean)
- fresh-context review subagent over the whole diff: found the new test fixture's three files were byte copies of the seed run.sh, which git diff -C treats as copies with no added lines; fixed by giving them distinct content. Also adopted its nit: a missing status with batch exit 0 now says 'reported…
- The lane run: https://github.com/melodic-software/claude-code-plugins/actions/runs/45624484385

Left out: the items under Not verified.

## Related

#18577
